Your coding agent asks. 
You answer from anywhere.

When your agent needs your call (a stack, a layout, an API key), it sends you a link instead of waiting at the terminal. You answer from your phone, alone or with your team. It reads the answers as JSON and gets back to work.

One prompt, one form

You ask once. It sends everything it needs to know.

Your agent puts every question in one form, its own picks pre-selected and the mockups to choose from. You answer where you are, it carries on.

Why not just ask in the terminal?

Your agent can already ask. Here’s what a form changes.

The same questions, answered somewhere better than a blinking prompt.

In the terminalWith ask-form
Where you answerAt the keyboard. Step away and the agent waits.Any browser, phone included. The agent keeps working meanwhile.
How many questionsA few at a time, turn after turn.Twenty at once, in pages, with its picks pre-selected.
Who answersYou, at that keyboard.Anyone with the link: a team vote, a client sign-off, beta testers. Every answer comes back, with an email field to know who said what.
What you seeText.Mockups to pick from, diagrams, tables and code.
What it gets back“1b, yes, the second one”, to interpret.JSON, keyed by question.
SecretsPasted into the chat and kept in the transcript.Written straight to .env. The model never sees them.

Try it on your setup

One sentence to your agent.

Any coding agent running on your computer will do. It reads /agent-install, installs ask-form, sets itself up and sends you a first form.

Paste this into your coding agent

Finish the sentence with what you want to be asked. Not a chat app such as claude.ai or ChatGPT: its sandbox can’t keep ask-form running.

Fetch {{ORIGIN}}/agent-install and follow it to install the ask-form skill and set it up, then ask me with it: what you want to be asked
Manual install

Linux and macOS, x86-64 or arm64. One command installs the binary in ~/.local/bin, connects your machine to this relay, starts the background service and adds the Claude Code skill.

curl -fsSL {{ORIGIN}}/install.sh | sh
  • Without the relay (forms answerable on this machine only): curl -fsSL {{ORIGIN}}/install.sh | sh -s -- --local
  • With Go 1.22+: go install github.com/GabrielVidal1/ask-form/cmd/ask-form@latest, then ask-form setup
  • Or take a binary from GitHub Releases, then run ask-form setup

The service installs new releases by itself (ASK_FORM_AUTO_UPGRADE=notify or off stops that). ask-form uninstall removes the service and the skill. Other agents than Claude Code: ask-form skill print --body >> AGENTS.md.

Private by design

Your forms never leave your machine.

  • Forms stay on your machineThe relay only passes page requests through. It stores no form and no answer.
  • One private link per formA 256-bit token. Answered once then closed, or open to your whole team until you close it. Every form expires.
  • Secrets go to .envA secret field's value never appears in the answers the agent reads.

Same 404 for an unknown form and a wrong token, no referrer, no cache, no indexing, a strict CSP, mockups in sandboxed script-free frames. More in how it works.
